To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report a nanostructure electrode for methanol electro oxidation by means of the cosputtering deposition method and that the three-phase electrode has improved electro catalytic activity in comparison to pure Pt and two- phase electrodes because of both the catalysis of tungstencarbide and size-control of tungsten oxide.
the three-phase electrode of Pt-WC-W0(3) nanostructure is more active and durable for methanol electro-oxidation than pure Pt electrode.

the co-sputtered Pt-WC-WC(3) three phase electrode has higher I (f) / I (b) and oxidation current in comparison with those for the pure Pt and two phase electrodes because of both the catalytic effect of tungsten carbides and size control by tungsten oxides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of nanostructured Pt-WC-Wo(3) three phase catalysts by co-sputtering method.
the development of a novel nanostructured electrode for the electrocatalytic methanol oxidation reaction.
a new method of synthesizing nanostructure electrodes by means of the sputtering deposition method for the electrocatalytic oxidation of methanol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synergistic effect of nanostructure and the three-phase electrode can be a promising approach for electrocatalysis of fuel cell reactions.
the synergism of tungsten carbides with platinum in a nanostructure is a very effective approach for the electrochemical oxidation of methanol.
the co-sputtered Pt-WC-W(3) three phase electrode has higher electrocatalytic performance than pure Pt and two phase electrodes for methanol oxidation reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three-phase electrode has the highest electrochemical activity and the best stability for methanol electro-oxidation among all electrodes.
the synergistic effects of tungsten oxide and carbide are very effective for improving electrocatalytic performance of the Pt-based catalysts for methanol oxidation.

the three-phase electrodes have the highest electrocatalytic activities among all the nanostructured electrodes for methanol oxidation, which is due to the synergistic effect between tungsten carbide, tungsten oxide and platinum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the co-sputtered nanostructured electrode has higher electrocatalytic activities than the conventional Pt electrode, which is attributed to the synergy effect of the three phases.
we can control the size and shape of the catalyst by using the co-sputtered tungsten oxide as a support.
the synergistic effect between the nanostructure electrodes and the catalytic effect of tungsten carbides can be used to improve methanol electrooxidative reaction activity.
